extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and general readers interested in the philosophy of humor and laughter
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive/anthological overview of classical and contemporary theories about laughter and humor, surveying historical accounts (Plato, Aristotle, Hobbes, Kant, Schopenhauer, Freud, etc.) and exploring aesthetics, ethics, and relations to other mental states. The page is a publisher book listing for an edited volume that collects sources and essays on these topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of traditional theories of laughter and humor
rubrics_metrics.description: This book assesses the adequacy of the traditional theories of laughter and humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The volume examines whether longstanding theories (superiority, incongruity, relief) adequately explain laughter and amusement, and it suggests revised theories where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superiority theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter is an expression of feelings of superiority over another person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical origin: held by Plato, Aristotle, and Hobbes. The book presents historical examples and discussion of this view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incongruity theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter is often a reaction to the perception of some incongruity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted by Aristotle and Cicero and later developed by Kant and Schopenhauer into a fuller incongruity account; the book presents these developments and their implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter is the venting of superfluous nervous energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associated with Herbert Spencer and Freud; the book discusses historical formulations and examples of the relief/venting account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid theories of laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: Hybrid or mixed accounts combining elements of the major theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes hybrid theories such as those of Descartes and Bergson; the book surveys alternative and mixed approaches rather than treating the major theories as mutually exclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetics of humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploration of the place of humor in aesthetics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book features traditional explorations of how humor functions aesthetically, including its role in drama and literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics of humor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers moral dimensions of laughter and what is permissible or blameworthy in comedic expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of amusement to other mental states
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of how amusement relates to other mental states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The volume looks at connections between amusement and emotions, cognition, and other psychological states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of classical sources and contemporary theories
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of both classic sources in the philosophy of humor and theories by contemporary philosophers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher claims this is the first work in fifty years to include classic sources alongside contemporary contributions, making the collection useful for historical and modern study.
